title: Book Two · Chapter 182: A Story with No Marks
story:
Ronan borrows a story about a boy and an old boat. There are no questions at the end. He looks twice to make sure.

At home, the small wooden boat from his own childhood sits on the shelf. Its two ends still have different colours. He takes it down and brushes dust from the bottom.

Dad passes the doorway.

“Going to the river?” he asks.

“Only in a book.”

“Less water on your shoes.”

Ronan puts the boat beside him and opens the story. The boy in the book wants to cross a river. His boat has a hole. An older man tells him to wait until it is fixed, but the boy wants to go first.

Ronan stops there. He thinks he knows the next part. The boat will fill with water. The boy will learn to listen.

He turns the page.

The boy does listen. He stays on the bank and gets angry instead. He watches his sister cross on a different boat. Then he helps fix his own.

Ronan reads that page more slowly. The boy is still angry. Ronan likes that part of the story. The old man is also wrong about one piece of wood. They need to change it together.

Mum calls him for a small job. She wants to measure some cloth. Ronan needs to hold the edge still. He puts a scrap of paper at his place and goes to help.

“Good story?” she asks.

“Better than I thought.”

“You look cross.”

“The boy is cross. I am borrowing his face.”

She smiles and measures the cloth. “Keep the edge still with it.”

When the job is done, Ronan returns to the book. He finishes the chapter about the repair. He wants to tell Leo the surprising part, but he wants Leo to read it first too.

The next day, he takes the book to school. At lunch, he starts to offer it to Leo. Then he remembers the school borrowing card.

“I can return it on Friday,” he says. “You can borrow it after me.”

Leo reads the cover. “Is the boat fast?”

“Not yet.”

“That is an honest answer.”

Ronan smiles. He puts the book safely away. He has a few pages left. He does not want to rush through them.

That evening, Dad asks how the river crossing goes. Ronan tells him that he does not know yet. Dad sits nearby with a work slip. For a while, they each read their own page. The little wooden boat stands between the books, dry and quiet on the table.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

childhood＝童年；bank＝河岸；cross＝生气的；rush＝匆忙赶完。

## 理解问题

1. 书中情节和Ronan预想的有什么不同？
2. 他为什么没有立即把借来的书转借给Leo？

## 读句子

**The boy does listen.**

拆开看：The boy / does listen.

那个男孩／确实听了劝。
